newsitem.title: UK: Top heavy dollar sags in late Europe, lira wobbles.
newsitem.headline: Top heavy dollar sags in late Europe, lira wobbles.

text.p: The dollar sagged against the yen in late European trading after a strong run up to 33-month highs at 112.90, although the yen was suffering after Sunday's general election in Japan, dealers said.
The market was banking profits on the dollar as it was looking a little overbought after recent gains.
"It was looking top heavy," said David Coleman, chief economist at CIBC Wood Gundy.
"It had a cracking run last week and a pretty good run the week before. The lack of any further good news to drive it up has seen it run out of steam."
At 1539 GMT dollar/yen was at 112.72/77 after the early 112.90 and previous close of 112.43/53. Dollar/mark was at 1.5361/66 after a 1.5435 high and previous 1.5412/22.

The lira was today's other notable feature which eased after Bundesbank council member Klaus-Dieter Kuehbacher cast fresh doubt on Italy's ability to join European economic and monetary union from 1999.

At 1554 GMT mark/lira was at 997.10/7.50 against 995.70/6.05 in late European trading on Friday, but below the session high of 998.20 which was hit in the immediate aftermath of Kuehbacher's comments.
The yen was also down elsewhere at 73.36/39 per mark versus Friday's 72.97/73.00.

Analysts said the inconclusive Japanese election result did little to change the political outlook in Japan and with fiscal policy now seen remaining on hold and the Bank of Japan unlikely to change its low interest rate policy for the time being.
Japan's Liberal Democratic Party recorded an expected strong showing but remained 12 seats short of an overall majority.
Traders warned about getting too carried away on the bear yen tack noting that, while there was no clear election result, opposition parties looked in disarray and were no real threat.
Analysts said it was likely the Japanese government would go ahead with planned sales tax rises in April so there would be no need for the Bank of Japan to tighten soon.

High-yielders stepped into the limelight again with the New Zealand dollar rallying to an eight-year high at 71.40 U.S. cents and the Australian dollar punching up to a four-year high against the yen and a five-year high on a trade weighted basis.
German M3 money growth came in broadly in line with forecasts but analysts said the underlying tone still looked fairly positive for the German, and European, interest rate markets.

The Bundesbank said the annualised rate of M3 growth slowed to 8.4 percent from 8.7 percent in August, which was within the range of forecasts of between 8.2 and 8.5 percent. The central bank said that slower bank lending and better capital formation contributed to the slowdown in M3 growth.

"Our early forecast is that overall M3 will grow an annualised 8.1 percent in October and that it will end the year just above the 4.0 to 7.0 percent target range," said Jeremy Hawkins, senior economic adviser at BankAmerica.
"This should keep market hopes for a further repo easing alive."
Sterling zipped higher in early trade but ran into profit-taking later, finishing at 2.4430/40 and $1.5912/19 after earlier highs of 2.4560 and $1.5950.
While its uptrend still looks intact, chartists warn of overbought conditions.

Against the mark, the 14-day relative strength index (RSI) is at 83 percent, way above the overbought watershed of 70 percent. On cable, the RSI is also in overbought territory at 74 percent, analysts noted.
Phil Smith, London Forex desk +44-171-542-6284.
